title: GPU fleet throttle rootcause hypotheses - postmortem data pull
summary: Data pull to support postmortem for intermittent throttling across EU-West and US-West on 2026-11-29. Focused on request-level signals (queue depth, throttle markers, KV cache evictions) and fleet state (GPU util, pod restarts, region headroom) to test three root-cause hypotheses.
objective: Produce a compact, query-first sheet that teams can use to validate or refute candidate root causes. Provide event-level joins, aggregated pivots by region/hour/model/tier, and sample trace examples for debugging rollout logic and autoscaler interactions.
approach: 1) Pull request-level telemetry for 48-hours around incident window. 2) Join with fleet control-plane events (scale up/down, preemptions, node restarts). 3) Compute derived signals (normalized queue depth, throttle-rate per-GPU, eviction-rate). 4) Surface top anomalous tenants and models for targeted replay and eval.
raw_queries:
-- Request-level slice: bigquery style
SELECT timestamp, region, zone, gpu_type, instance_id, tenant_id, model_name, request_id, seq_len, tokens_generated, batch_size, is_streaming, kv_cache_hit, queue_depth, throttle_flag, throttle_reason, latency_ms, p95_latency_ms FROM telemetry.requests WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-11-28') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-11-30') AND (throttle_flag = TRUE OR queue_depth > 10)

-- Fleet events: control plane (k8s events + autoscaler)
SELECT event_ts, event_type, region, node_id, gpu_capacity_change, reason, linked_scale_id FROM control_plane.events WHERE event_ts BETWEEN '2026-11-28' AND '2026-11-30'

-- Pod restarts + OOMs (ClickHouse)
SELECT ts, region, node, pod, reason, exit_code FROM infra.node_events WHERE reason LIKE '%OOM%' OR reason LIKE '%Restart%' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-11-28' AND '2026-11-30'

-- KV cache eviction telemetry
SELECT ts, region, model_name, tenant_id, eviction_count, total_kv_size_bytes FROM caching.kv_metrics WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-11-28' AND '2026-11-30'

-- Derived aggregation: per-region per-hour throttle rate
SELECT region, HOUR(timestamp) as hour, COUNTIF(throttle_flag)/COUNT(*) as throttle_rate, AVG(queue_depth) as avg_q_depth, PERCENTILE_CONT(latency_ms, 0.95) as latency_p95 FROM telemetry.requests WHERE timestamp BETWEEN '2026-11-28' AND '2026-11-30' GROUP BY region, hour ORDER BY region, hour

-- Top offending tenants by throttle volume
SELECT tenant_id, region, model_name, COUNT(*) as throttle_count, AVG(batch_size) as avg_batch, SUM(tokens_generated) as tokens FROM telemetry.requests WHERE throttle_flag = TRUE AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-11-29' AND '2026-11-29 23:59:59' GROUP BY tenant_id, region, model_name ORDER BY throttle_count DESC LIMIT 50

observations: Preliminary joins show two distinct signatures during the event window: (A) localized spikes in queue_depth and throttle_flag that map to short-lived node restarts in eu-west1, often preceded by KV cache eviction bursts; (B) broader region-level throttle increases with no corresponding node events but coincident with autoscaler cooldown windows in US-West. Latency p95 correlates strongly with queue depth for signature A; signature B shows rising throttle_rate before p95 moves drastically.
hypotheses: Hypothesis 1: KV cache eviction cascade — sudden eviction bursts (large models + many tenants warming) caused cache misses that amplified request latencies and produced queue backpressure; manifests as eviction_count spikes shortly before throttle events and node OOM/restarts.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler hysteresis + burst arrivals — autoscaler cooldowns prevented capacity from catching up to short bursts, causing sustained queueing at region level; manifests as throttle_rate climbing across the region while individual nodes remain healthy.

Hypothesis 3: Scheduler packing/affinity regression — a deployment change in the scheduler increased co-location density on some nodes leading to momentary GPU oversubscription and higher pod restart counts; manifests as correlated pod_restart_count and increased per-node in_flight despite nominal reported capacity.

Hypothesis 4: Traffic shaping / tenant misconfiguration — a small number of tenants sent large batched bulk requests (high batch_size, high tokens_generated) that congested local queues and evicted KV caches for shared models.

Hypothesis 5: Regional network hiccup — transient egress/backhaul latency caused slowed worker-heartbeats leading to temporary inaccurate capacity signals and aggressive throttling by the router layer (no node events but region-level throttle upticks).
action_items: 1) Run targeted replays for top 10 tenants from sample_rows on a local staging fleet with KV cache enabled to reproduce eviction signature (owner: Maya).
2) Correlate autoscaler decision logs with throttle_rate timeline and add a short-term metric alert for 'throttle_rate > 1% for 5m during autoscaler cooldown' (owner: Liam).
3) Capture extended debug traces (router + serving runtime) for next 7 days for models in top offending list and enable 1% debug sampling for these tenants (owner: Sofia).
4) Add a control-plane runbook to detect cache-eviction cascades: alert when eviction_count / total_kv_size increases > 300% within 10m and throttle_rate > 0.5% (owner: Jamal).
5) Follow-up: schedule a scheduler-snapshot audit to review recent packing changes in the last 30 days and roll back if density anomalies are found (owner: infra-scheduling team).
